name: GET /api/leadflow/identity/review-queue - steward case queue with risk bands, ages and EMPI metrics
description:
The one call behind the Identity Review screen (#view-identity): the open candidate links a steward has to adjudicate, the six KPI tiles above them, and the review SLA the ages are measured against.

COMPOSED SERVER-SIDE, ONE CALL PER SCREEN. sdk-identity-resolver's candidate-link list and its EMPI metrics are read concurrently and joined here rather than fanned out from the browser, so the screen cannot render a queue and a set of counters that disagree about the same instant.

SORTED BY RISK THEN AGE, AND THAT SORT IS OURS. Upstream orders by `confidence DESC` and nothing else (queryCandidateLinksByBand). Confidence descending is NOT risk-then-age: two high-risk cases an hour apart come back in confidence order, so the older one can sit below a newer one that is fractionally more confident. The queue therefore re-sorts by band first and `created_at` ascending within the band, which is the order a steward works in - hardest and longest-waiting first.

RISK BANDS MIRROR THE UPSTREAM THRESHOLDS, they are not re-invented here: high >= 0.9, medium 0.7 to 0.9, low below 0.7, copied from bandRange() in empiService.ts. A screen that drew its own boundaries would disagree with the service that queued the case, and the operator would be told a case is medium while the resolver treats it as high.

THREE OF THE SIX TILES HAVE NO UPSTREAM SOURCE AND SAY SO. EmpiMetrics carries unresolved_candidate_links, merge_reversals, total_merges, calibration_ece, confidence_distribution and drift_alert - and nothing else. So Review Cases, Retracted Links and Resolver Calibration are live, while Exact Auto-Links, Kept Separate and Median Review have no metric behind them: each returns null with a `metric_gaps` entry naming what is missing. A dash the operator can ask about is worth more than a plausible number nobody can source, and inventing 'median review time' from the age of OPEN cases would be the most dangerous option of the three - it reads as a service level and would be measuring the opposite, since a queue nobody has worked yet has a rising median that looks like fast service.

DEGRADES TO AN HONEST 200 PER PANEL. Each upstream read answers independently, so metrics being down empties the tiles and leaves the queue usable rather than failing the screen. upstream_available reports each read separately, and an empty queue is never conflated with an unreachable one.

requiresRole:["data_steward"] and NO testCase pins an Authorization header. identity.merge_review is REUSED rather than a new identity.review_read invented: it already exists, the Data Steward is the only role holding it, and reading this queue is the same authority as adjudicating from it - the queue IS the merge-review surface. A separate read grant would let more people look at a probabilistic claim about two real people than are trusted to settle it, which is the wrong way round. The suite's default identity bridges to sales_rep and would only see 403, so the runner swaps to testCredentials.data_steward; a pinned header would take PRECEDENCE over that token and defeat the swap (MUST-71). The 401 cases are therefore documented in errorCases rather than authored.

THE HAPPY PATH IS THE DEGRADED 200, and expectedStatus says so rather than describing an environment that does not exist. Nothing in LeadFlow creates a candidate link - they are raised inside sdk-identity-resolver's probabilistic matcher - so there is no producer to chain from and no seeded case to read. What the suite observes is the composed envelope with upstream_available:false and empty collections, which is a real branch worth holding: it proves the screen degrades per panel instead of erroring. Point this at an environment with a populated EMPI and the same call returns the populated queue the description above describes. QA: depends on register and login.

testCases.name: The composed queue answers with per-panel availability rather than an error
NEGATIVE: an unknown risk band is rejected rather than silently ignored

errorCases.message: band must be one of high, medium, low
errorCases.when: an unrecognised band is supplied. Dropping it would return the WHOLE queue to a steward who asked for one slice, and reading that as 'these are the high-risk cases' is exactly the misreading this screen must not cause.

errorCases.message: Authorization header with a bearer token is required
errorCases.when: the Authorization header is absent, empty, or uses a scheme other than Bearer. Not authored as a testCase: it can only be expressed by pinning a header, which would defeat the role swap (MUST-71).

errorCases.message: Session token is invalid or expired
errorCases.when: a Bearer token was presented but does not verify. Not authored, for the same reason as above.

errorCases.message: No policy grants this action to the caller's roles.
errorCases.when: the caller's roles do not grant identity.merge_review, which the Data Steward alone holds. NOT reachable while this definition runs under requiresRole, and kept because it is the real branch the default suite identity receives.
